explanation: Count the exact characters required by the letter. Spend one needed occurrence for each matching magazine character. The letter is constructible exactly when every needed occurrence has been supplied; spaces and case remain significant.
timeComplexity: O(L + M) expected time for letter and magazine lengths. Each letter and magazine character makes one expected-constant-time count update.
spaceComplexity: O(u + M) auxiliary space: u distinct letter-character counts plus magazineText.toCharArray(), which materializes M characters.

correctness: The frequency map contains exactly the positive unsupplied letter counts. Matching a magazine occurrence decrements one count and deletes a key at zero, so no magazine character is used twice. An empty map is equivalent to supplying every letter occurrence; any remaining positive count proves failure.
walkthrough: For letter "Bee!" and magazine "eB!e?", consume one e, then B, then !, then the second e. Nothing remains needed, and the unused ? is harmless, so return true.
edgeCases: An empty letter is always constructible.
Extra magazine characters do not invalidate a successful construction.
